newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli farmer kills Palestinian worker.
newsitem.headline: Israeli farmer kills Palestinian worker.

text.p: An Israeli farmer shot and killed a Palestinian worker who he suspected was trying to break into his house in southern Israel before dawn on Thursday, a police spokeswoman said.

The farmer, aged 56, was detained for questioning over the shooting in Kochav Michael village, a day after Arab gunmen killed a Jewish woman settler and her 12-year-old son in a roadside ambush in the occupied West Bank, the spokeswoman said.

"He said he heard strange voices coming from outside. He said he thought somebody was trying to break in. So he took his gun and went outside and fired at them. They tried to flee but one of them fell," the policewoman said.
She said the shooting was from a distance of a few metres (yards) and it appeared the slain Palestinian had once worked for his killer.

Israel's domestic news agency Itim said the farmer initially told police he believed the Gazan worker was a burglar but later contended he suspected the Palestinian was a "terrorist" about to carry out an attack.
"I heard voices in Arabic and thought they were terrorists. I shouted at them to stop. They ran away and then I shot," Itim quoted the farmer as telling police investigators.

Itim reported the dead man was one of three Palestinians brought to the village from Gaza in the early morning by the farmer's neighbour. It said they were walking towards the fields when the shots rang out.
Ziad al-Atrash, a senior Palestinian police officer in Gaza, told Reuters: "I don't want to pre-empt events, but the information I have does not match the claim that the workers were on a robbery."
Atrash, head of the Palestinian side of a joint liaison committee with Israel, said he had asked Israeli authorities to set up a joint team to investigate the case.
